hits.snippet: Israeli cybersecurity company [Oligo Security](https://www.linkedin.com/company/oligo-security/) has secured $60 million in a new funding round after reporting sharp revenue growth and a doubling of its valuation since its Series B financing. The round was backed by Ballistic Ventures, Greenfield Partners, Red Dot Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners and TLV Partners. Investors Yasmin Lukatz and Eyal Waldman also participated. The company plans to use the capital to speed up product innovation and strengthen its presence in markets outside Israel. hits.title: Oligo Security raises $60 million to expand runtime protection as AI speeds up exploit development
hits.snippet: Runtime security startup Oligo Security has raised $60 million in new funding to accelerate product innovation and expand global go-to-market operations. The round, announced today, comes as attackers increasingly use AI to find vulnerabilities and build exploits at machine speed, making runtime protection a critical line of defense for production systems. ### How Oligo's runtime approach works Oligo's software sits alongside applications in production. A sensor built on [eBPF](https://ebpf.io/?ref=completeaitraining.com), the Linux kernel feature, tracks which library functions a workload actually calls. Most vulnerabilities flagged by scanners are never called at all, and Oligo tells customers they can leave those alone. The ones that do get called can be blocked mid-exploit at the application layer, without killing the container or the process behind it. That last capability arrived in April with Runtime Exploit Blocking, which defends against classes of attack techniques rather than individual CVEs. hits.snippet: [OLIGO Security](https://www.oligo.security/), the runtime security company, has raised $60m in fresh funding as it races to help organisations keep pace with attacks that are now being planned and executed by AI at machine speed. The round takes OLIGO’s total funding to $140m and drew backing from Ballistic Ventures, Canon Capital, Greenfield Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Red Dot Capital Partners and TLV Partners, alongside angel investors including Eyal Waldman, the co-founder of Mellanox Technologies, which NVIDIA acquired for $6.9bn. The company said the raise caps a strong year of growth, with revenue climbing 300% year-on-year and its valuation more than doubling since its Series B. Over the same period, OLIGO was named by AWS as its exclusive AI runtime security partner for AWS Security Hub Extended, and it joined Palantir’s FedStart Programme to speed up its route to FedRAMP High and DoD Impact Level 5 authorisation. The firm also launched Runtime Exploit Blocking, a capability that detects and stops exploit attempts at the application layer as they happen. hits.title: OLIGO Security Raises $60 Million, Bringing Total Funding To $140 Million
hits.snippet: OLIGO Security has raised $60 million in additional funding, bringing the runtime cybersecurity company’s total funding to $140 million. Participants included Ballistic Ventures, Canon Capital, Greenfield Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Red Dot Capital Partners and TLV Partners. The round also included angel investors such as Mellanox Technologies (acquired by NVIDIA for $6.9 billion) co-founder Eyal Waldman. OLIGO plans to use the capital to accelerate product development, expand its global go-to-market operations and advance its technology for blocking zero-day and known vulnerability exploits in real time. The company provides runtime security across applications, cloud workloads and AI systems. Its platform monitors code while it is executing, helping customers identify vulnerabilities that can actually be exploited and block attacks without disrupting production environments. OLIGO said the platform can reduce vulnerability alert noise and provide virtual patching capabilities between conventional software patch cycles. The financing follows a period in which OLIGO reported 300% year-over-year revenue growth and more than doubled its valuation since its Series B round.
